admission_rule.algorithm_must_be_named: a recorded digest must state the algorithm that produced it, in the field name or in an adjacent digest_algorithm/hash_algorithm field
admission_rule.algorithm_must_be_admitted: a stated algorithm must appear in admitted_algorithms before a record may carry it
admission_rule.length_must_match: a value whose length cannot be the digest it names is reported, not repaired
admission_rule.existing_records: existing unnamed records are a migration population; no record was edited to add an algorithm

admitted_algorithms.rationale: the content digest used by the package manifest, the receipts and every evidence record that hashes bytes; it is not a repository object id and is not the object-id algorithm

subject_path_keyed.statement: these keys are subjects (file paths); the value is a digest of the subject and the algorithm is unnamed

absent_markers.statement: a field names a digest algorithm but holds an explicit absence marker; the digest was never recorded, which is a gap rather than a migration item

mislabelled_length.statement: a value whose length cannot be the digest it names is reported, not repaired

named_key_with_non_digest_value.statement: a key naming an algorithm whose value is not a hex digest is reported; it may be a constant or a length, not a digest

repository_object_ids.statement: these values are repository object ids under object-identity keys. They belong to the repository-identity system, not the content-digest system, and are excluded from every digest population above. Their length alone does not identify them: a 64-hex value could be either a sha256 object id or a SHA-256 content digest, and only the declaring key separates them

migration_population.statement: records that do not name their digest algorithm are recorded here as a population to migrate; no existing record was edited to add an algorithm

what_is_rehashed: the source tree at a new candidate, with the new algorithm alongside the old digest
each content-addressed artefact named by a receipt (archive, measurement DSO, distribution DSO, consumer binaries)
the ETP-6 package manifest and the frozen Git object store it names
the claim evidence entries that bind an artefact to an identity
how_the_old_relationship_is_preserved: the original record is retained byte-for-byte and its original algorithm is named in the renewal record
the renewal record names renewal_of with the old algorithm and digest, and the new algorithm and digest
a renewed commitment is a new record; it is never substituted for the original
the versioned schema identifier is bumped only when the shape changes, not when an algorithm is added
what_is_never_rewritten: Git object identities and commit hashes
historical receipts, including withdrawn ones and their withdrawal records
the original digest algorithm named by a historical record
the ETP-0 claim inventory and other source documents of a completed migration
a timestamp or a signature over old material, which a later signature cannot retroactively validate
renewal_plan.trigger: a new authenticated commitment is recorded before an existing algorithm is treated as inadequate; the original and the renewal are both preserved
renewal_plan.trusted_time_assumption: a renewal inherits the trust in the old record's time and does not retroactively establish it; the original timestamp and the renewal timestamp are both retained
renewal_plan.statement: the population is not migrated: this is the stated plan for renewing every record, and it never rewrites the old relationship

renewal_records.subject: evidence/etp0/CLAIMS.json
renewal_records.renewal_reason: demonstration of a digest-agility binding; no algorithm is being retired by this record
renewal_records.trusted_time_assumption: the renewal inherits the trust placed in the original record's time and does not retroactively establish it; the original timestamp and the renewal time are both recorded
renewal_records.statement: old and new digests are computed over the same archived bytes; the old binding is preserved rather than replaced, and the object id is recorded separately because it is not a content digest

renewal_records.subject: forensics/etp6/verify.sh
renewal_records.renewal_reason: demonstration of a digest-agility binding; no algorithm is being retired by this record
renewal_records.trusted_time_assumption: the renewal inherits the trust placed in the original record's time and does not retroactively establish it; the original timestamp and the renewal time are both recorded
renewal_records.statement: old and new digests are computed over the same archived bytes; the old binding is preserved rather than replaced, and the object id is recorded separately because it is not a content digest

renewal_verification.method: verify_renewal recomputes the old and new digest over the archived bytes named by each record
renewal_verification.statement: each renewal binds two algorithms over one identical archived byte sequence. A record whose old or new digest covers different bytes is refused; the verifier cannot tell which side was altered, so it refuses the pair

identity_separation.statement: a repository object id and a content digest are different systems. A value is assigned to the object-identity system only when its key names an object identity; every other digest-shaped value is a content digest claim
